answer: No—not by itself. A recorded supervision event or completed reconciliation may evidence an activity, but does not establish its adequacy or that ownership records properly reflect investors’ rights. That conclusion requires an applicable substantive standard and evidence of the activity’s scope, quality, findings and follow-up over the relevant period. The retained provisions supply qualitative requirements, not a rule deeming either event sufficient.

claims.inference: The text distinguishes continuing responsibility and proper records from the occurrence of a particular control activity. It follows that an event log alone cannot establish fulfillment.
missing_premises: The retained edition applies to the identified product, Product Provider, activity and assessment period, taking account of applicable conditions and modifications.
An applicable interpretation of operational soundness and proper ownership records.
Evidence showing the actual arrangement and records satisfy that standard throughout the relevant period.
claims.proposition: Paragraphs 10 and 11 require substantive responsibility and proper records; they do not make recorded activity a sufficient discharge test.
claims.status: Text-supported requirement; deduction about evidential insufficiency

support.quote: Product Providers should remain and be ultimately responsible for the management and operational soundness of the tokenisation arrangement adopted and record keeping of ownership, regardless of any outsourcing arrangement1.

Product Providers should ensure that proper records of token holders’ ownership interests in the product are maintained and the tokenisation arrangement is operationally compatible with service providers involved2.

claims.inference: Where UT 6.11C applies, one logged event does not by itself prove ongoing monitoring, supervision or periodic review. Applying that valuation-specific standard to other outsourced activities would require a separate legal justification.
missing_premises: The entity is the relevant management company and the third party performs valuation within UT 6.11C.
Applicable authorization conditions, modifications or relaxations and a justified assessment of reasonable care, skill and diligence.

Evidence of reviewer competence, review scope and frequency, information examined, deficiencies identified, escalation and corrective follow-up. These are proposed evidential inquiries, not an express exhaustive checklist in the quoted text.
claims.proposition: A supervision record must be assessed against the relevant actor-specific and activity-specific standard, not treated as proof of adequate supervision.
claims.status: Conditional textual standard; proposed factual assessment

support.quote: Where a third party is engaged in the valuation of a scheme, the management company shall exercise reasonable care, skill and diligence in the selection, appointment and ongoing monitoring of such third party in ensuring such entity possesses the appropriate level of knowledge, experience and resources that commensurate with the appropriate valuation policies and procedures for each scheme.
The valuation activities of such third party should be subject to ongoing supervision and periodic review by the management company.
This UT Code does not have the force of law.

claims.inference: The Appendix treats regular reconciliation as a consideration alongside legal validity and encumbrances. Completion of one reconciliation does not establish regularity, accuracy or legal entitlement; matching records could share an error.
missing_premises: A justified determination that the Appendix factors apply to this arrangement.
The legally effective ownership interests, governing law, settlement finality and any encumbrances.
Evidence identifying the records compared, their completeness and reliability, reconciliation frequency and coverage, discrepancies and their resolution.
A justified standard connecting those findings to proper records under paragraph 11.
claims.proposition: Reconciliation is relevant evidence of record quality, but completion alone is not proof of proper ownership records.
claims.status: Text-supported relevance; deduction and proposed factual inquiries

support.quote: For factors of consideration, please also refer to Part A of the Appendix to the Tokenised Securities Circular, where applicable, when formulating the tokenisation arrangement.

For example, whether the ownership interest of the underlying assets of the Tokenised Securities are legally valid under the applicable governing laws, whether there are regular reconciliations between the records for the extrinsic rights and the records for the distributed ledger tokens, or whether any encumbrance affects the extrinsic rights.

claims.inference: Assigning register maintenance to an appointed person does not remove the Product Provider’s retained responsibility. Neither allocation establishes actual maintenance or record quality.
missing_premises: The actual scheme, trustee, appointed register keeper and Product Provider roles and their legal relationships.
Evidence of valid appointment, actual maintenance and records that reflect investors’ ownership.
A supported standard for deciding whether the Product Provider fulfilled its retained responsibility.
claims.proposition: Allocation of functions, performance of activities and substantive fulfillment require separate findings.

support.quote: The scheme, or in the case of a unit trust, the trustee or the person so appointed by the trustee must maintain a register of holders.
the Product Provider should remain fully responsible, despite any outsourcing arrangement such as those envisaged under 6.8 of the Code on Unit Trusts and Mutual Funds.

rival_readings: An allocation-focused reading emphasizes retained ultimate responsibility despite delegation; it does not establish that supervision or records are adequate.

A conduct-focused reading asks whether the provider exercised appropriate oversight. UT 6.11C expressly supplies a conduct standard for outsourced valuation, but its transfer to other activities remains conditional.

An outcome-focused or combined reading emphasizes operational soundness and proper ownership records as well as responsibility and conduct. The retained text does not settle a universal discharge test or establish strict liability for every adverse outcome.
unresolved: No actual supervision record, reconciliation results, ownership documentation or assessment interval is supplied.
The applicable qualitative standard, required evidential coverage and consequences of deficiencies remain undetermined.
Absence of sufficient evidence establishes neither fulfillment nor breach. Candidate rules or solver acceptance cannot supply the missing legal and factual premises.
